page: Microsoft Azure M416ms_v2 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server belonging to the MSv2 family. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8487C processors running at 4.0 GHz, providing 416 virtual CPUs across 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system features an L3 cache of 105 MB and is equipped with 11400.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 27.4 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 8389 GB SSD, and the instance is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics from stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests fall into the bottom 25%, the massive core count drives multi-core performance into the top 10% for stress-ng, PassMark CPU, and bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only small block speeds reaching 19469.58 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 320.33 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also highly competitive, with Redis achieving 290.37 million operations per second.

Given its massive memory footprint and high multi-core throughput, this server offers high resource density for workloads that can exploit parallel execution and large in-memory datasets. However, the weak single-core performance represents a tradeoff for single-threaded tasks. The M416ms_v2 is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational database management systems, massive Redis caching layers, and heavy data processing pipelines that require substantial RAM without GPU acceleration.
